messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — multiple serving nodes reporting OOM/CUDA errors and container restarts. Auto-page to oncall.
alice: seeing the same in dashboards. p50 latency fine but p99s and error rate spiked ~09:10 UTC. Observability shows KV cache miss storms and retransmit counters high.
ben: I can pull runtime logs. guess it's either kvcache thrash or IB packet loss causing replays.
carol: RNIC metrics show increased out_of_order and retransmit_on_wire on two racks.
ben: logs from a crashed container:
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:58Z] runtime: kvcache_eviction: 1223/sec
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] serving: cuda error: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (0x4)
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] containerd: SIGABRT
```
alice: customer 42 (api-heavy) reported 503s. support flagged a small but high-value set.
dave_oncall: I'm on it. handing to infra & net. @ben can you attach node IDs?
ben: nodes: rackB-node-07, rackB-node-08, rackC-node-02. kernel logs show IB QP errors:
```
mlx5_ib 0000:3b:00.1: pkey violation on QP 0x9a1f: pkt_seq 0x1f4 -> retransmit
rdma_retransmit: 76 events in last 60s
```
eve_sre: running `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide --selector=app=runtime` — several pods on those nodes restart_count > 3.
carol: checked switch counters: fabric reports ECN marks and RX retransmit ramp on ports 4/5 (rackB) and 10 (rackC). link-level CRCs minimal — looks like packet reorder rather than physical link flapping.
net-bot: netprobe alert: ibpathprobe failure between rackB-node-07 -> rackC-node-02, avg RTT 2.4ms -> spikes to 45ms and drops.
alice: correlation: when RTT spikes, kvcache misses increase and KV streaming tail latency balloons -> runtime hits GPU memory pressure and crashes.
ben: mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes to stop serving on bad fabric 2) shift traffic to dedicated fallback model variant 3) collect full rdma debug + tcpdump for infra.
dave_oncall: executing step 1 now. `kubectl cordon rackB-node-07 rackB-node-08 rackC-node-02` — starting drain for pods with graceful 30s.
carol: while drain runs, I'm toggling conservative batching and disabling prefetch across runtime to reduce KV cache churn.
eve_sre: started traffic shift rule on the router: all sessions with customer_tag=42 -> fallback-lowmem-model. will monitor.
ben: grabbing `ibv_devinfo` and `ethtool -S` from rackB-node-07:
```
ibv_devinfo: port 1: link state PORT_ERR
mlx5 driver stats: rx_no_buf 0, rx_queue_ovfl 0, rx_errors 0, rx_packets 1,234,567
rdma_retries_exceeded: 812
```
carol: interesting — driver shows retries_exceeded high but link up. could be microbursts on switch causing reorder and HW-level retransmits.
alice: customer impact: about 0.6% of requests for the cluster in the 09:10–09:18 window 503/504s, concentrated on that small set of nodes. support: notifying customers affected, adding incident banner.
dave_oncall: nodes drained. new pods scheduled on healthy racks. observing GC and memory usage on replacements.
ben: collecting tcpdump on port 4791 (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) for 60s and exporting to /tmp/rdma-pcap-1779995432.pcap.
carol: added temporary iproute qdisc to smooth egress: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel` on nodes being re-introduced. will prevent bursts.
eve_sre: traffic shifted successfully. error rate down from 1.8% -> 0.15% in last 2 mins.
net-bot: switch telemetry: ECN marking rate dropped after drains; retransmit rate falling.
ben: still seeing one container restart on rackC-node-05 unrelated — investigating but not tied to RDMA.
alice: next steps: keep nodes cordoned until we analyze pcap + run `ibdiagnet` and driver logs. open RM ticket with infra vendor for possible switch microburst behaviour.
dave_oncall: agree. handing to infra post-incident. I'm leaving pager to eve_sre for follow-up on customer comms.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated: partial (traffic shifted + drains). severity downgraded to Sev3. oncall handoff to infra for root-cause analysis.
ben: attaching quick timeline & data to the thread: pcap path, `/var/log/dmesg` extracts, rdma counters CSV.
alice: thanks all. will keep the postmortem stub in #postmortems and tag as rdma-retransmit-induced-runtime-crash.
carol: note for postmortem: include eval of KV cache eviction thresholds, batching settings, and whether we should auto-fallback earlier on retransmit surge.
end of thread.
